ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC=8$. Fold $\triangle ABC$ so that point A coincides with point D on side BC, with EF as the crease. If $AE=5$, what is the value of $\sin\angle BFD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and AC=BC=8, \\
it follows that $\angle A=\angle B$, \\
By the properties of folding: $\triangle AEF\cong \triangle DEF$, \\
Hence, $\angle EDF=\angle A$, \\
Thus, $\angle EDF=\angle B$, \\
Therefore, $\angle CDE+\angle BDF+\angle EDF=\angle BFD+\angle BDF+\angle B=180^\circ$, \\
Hence, $\angle CDE=\angle BFD$. \\
Moreover, since AE=DE=5, \\
it follows that CE=8−5=3, \\
Therefore, in right-angled $\triangle ECD$, $\sin\angle CDE= \frac{CE}{ED}=\frac{3}{5}$, \\
Therefore, $\sin\angle BFD=\boxed{\frac{3}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the figure is right triangle ABC, C is above, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right; E is located on side AC, D is located on side BC, F is located on side AB; the dashed line EF represents the crease, and A is folded to point D on BC. Then reason: Because ∠ACB=90° and AC=BC=8, △ABC is an isosceles right triangle, ∠A=∠B. The folding makes A coincide with D, and EF is the crease, therefore △AEF and △DEF are correspondingly congruent about the crease, so AE=DE, and ∠EDF=∠A. Also because ∠A=∠B, so ∠EDF=∠B. Since C, D, B are collinear, at point D there is ∠CDE+∠EDF+∠BDF=180°; while in △BDF, ∠BFD+∠BDF+∠B=180°. Comparing the two equations and ∠EDF=∠B, ∠CDE=∠BFD can be obtained. Given AE=5, so DE=5; also E is on AC, AC=8, therefore CE=AC−AE=8−5=3. △ECD is right-angled at C, so sin∠CDE=CE/DE=3/5. Because ∠CDE=∠BFD, so sin∠BFD=3/5.
